text:
lina: FYI a partner hit a nasty edge where a POST executed twice when a 429 landed right as the SDK was doing a token refresh. They saw duplicate billing. :(

alex: oof. do we have logs or a minimal repro? sounds like a race where the SDK retried while the refresh was still inflight.

lina: pasted log excerpt:
```
2024-09-03T09:12:01Z DEBUG request id=opQ status=429 retry-after=0.4
2024-09-03T09:12:01Z DEBUG auth refresh start for session=sk_live_xxx
2024-09-03T09:12:01Z DEBUG internal retry sent -> 200 (side-effect applied)
2024-09-03T09:12:02Z DEBUG auth refresh finished; draining queued requests -> 200 (side-effect applied)
```

vikram: yup, two successful side-effects. Root cause: Node SDK currently pumps retries immediately even if refresh hasn't finished; Py queued some requests so it's less likely to double-play. We need parity + safer defaults.

alex: design idea: when refresh in-progress, SDK should default to queuing mutating requests. If the request includes an explicit Idempotency-Key header we allow immediate send (leave dedupe to server). Config flag to opt-out: allow_immediate_replay=true.

lina: +1. Also handle 429 timing: if 429 happens before refresh, we should apply a mild jittered backoff rather than immediate retry. Suggested formula: delay = baseDelay * (1.6 ** attempt) * (0.7 + random() * 0.6)  # keeps variability high but bounded

nate: note: always honor Retry-After if provided. If Retry-After > 0.9s treat it as authoritative and don't attempt local replay until then.

maya: sampleapp changes: automatically add Idempotency-Key on write endpoints and expose `client.config.autoIdempotency = true` so integrators can toggle. Also add an e2e that simulates: 429 -> auth refresh start -> server accepts both replays -> final assertion: only one side-effect recorded.

vikram: test note: we should mock time and responses so test deterministically exercises the race. QA should assert telemetry increment for retries and for queued drains.

alex: telemetry: add metric sdk.replay.during_auth_refresh.count with tag sdk=js|py and sdk.replay.queued.count. Also emit a histogram of delay before replay to help tune jitter.

lina: for parity: I'll draft the Node change to enqueue by default; nate can replicate pattern in Py. We should add a short code comment explaining the tradeoff (queue vs immediate) so future contributors understand reasons.

nate: assigning: I'll take Node telemetry + tests. Vikram you take sampleapp e2e + docs. Lina you open the RFC with design and opt-in flag details. Maya will do customer comms.

ci-bot: CI queued: run/tests (node-sdk) #2304 by nate

alex: one more thought: for streaming/multipart requests we may need a different strategy (can't always pause). Let's flag streaming as follow-up and make sure to document behavior.

lina: agreed. adding a follow-up task in the RFC. timeline: patch for Node next week, Py parity the week after. We'll include the telemetry and the autoIdempotency opt-in in the patch.

maya: I'll update docs + support KB with recommended Idempotency-Key usage and a note about SDK config.

vikram: minor implementation detail: when draining queued requests, preserve original headers and retry count but don't replay if we detect server returned 2xx earlier for the same request id (if we can track it). We'll add safe-guard checks.

alex: thanks all. please link the RFC here when ready and tag eng-ml if kernel-level opts needed.

lina: will do. :thumbsup:
